item.description:

Diving data

  • Water type: Fresh

References

Portions of the following information were taken from www.protecsardinia.com The dry cave area of the Bue Marino system was opened to the public as a tourist attraction . In high summer, some boat operators travel here on a daily basis, to show the tourists the magnificent Stalactite formations. Right next to entrance, where the transport boats are moored, the dive starts. We descent to shallow water (1.50m), once inside we ascent to the surface in a large room. In this large hall you can still use the old stairs once used by tourists and explore the dry area of the cave safely. Our journey takes us underwater below a small bridge to the actual cave entrance of Bue Marino. Equipment check, safety drill, air planning and we are of into the cave system. The entrance area is a bit milky, maximum depth here is 15m. Fresh water flows through the cave entrance in the open which off course enhances the effect of the Halocline strongly (fresh and salt water mixing). Many sumps present themselves in this cave system and it is always worth it to accent and view the unbelievable beauty of the formations. The cave seems to be endless. Massive rooms or chambers showing beautiful formations. A part of this system goes up and down. There are many other tunnels in different connecting with the main tunnel. Some ending fairly soon in a dead end sump, others continue for several kilometres. There is a possibility to continue with a dry walk to the next sump and dive further. The dry passages on themselves are worth the dive. There is much to discover in this system! Equipment configuration: Back mount and Sidemount for the Sumps.

item.title: Ghost Cave
item.description:
About

Discovery

The discovery, made during a night dive in the summer of 1994, is due to Marco Busdraghi, who then carried out the first explorations and surveys, and who disseminated knowledge of it through the press and television. Busdraghi himself later also discovered the fossil deposit of sardinian deer in the Punta Giglio cave.

Description

The cave joint has a maximum penetration of approximately 70 meters. The different environments are characterized by an alternation of large openings and narrow passages with multiple aerial outcrops and an internal lake characterized by some “waterfalls” of very spectacular calcitic volutes. The submerged parts are particularly interesting for the modifying evolutions that occurred during the various geological eras which can be summarized in three very long distinct phases: a first phase was the typical one of the creation of caves in an aerial environment, with erosion/melting of the limestone due to the action of the waters, a second, again in an aerial environment, for the creation of numerous layers of calcite, in some parts above clay and mud deposits, and countless stalactites and stalagmites with also, thanks to the fusion of these, many joined columns, the third, more recent phase was that of “reerosion” of the cave of the submerged parts, therefore destroying all the spectacular calcite formations that have remained in the currently surface parts, both in the main lakes and in the numerous niches and outcrops. The calcite of this cave is white in color and semi-transparent, so much so that by placing a lamp in contact you obtain beautiful plays of light. In the swing line or shoreline the eroded calcite takes the resemblance of melting ice to warm water. The characteristic that makes it one of the most important caves in the Sardinia and of all the mediterranean basin in a scientific sense it is that of being a cave with Dolomite characteristics in a marine environment. Due to the particular nature of the waters, life inside, unlike almost all the other submerged caves in the area, is almost non-existent and therefore extremely clear, unless the sediment or some mud deposits scattered in various parts of the cave.

Diving data

References

Portions of the following information were taken from www.protecsardinia.com This entrance is spectacular. One dives into this system as if you were entering a Indonesian Temple. The bottom is covered with snow white sand and the inner walls get together in pyramid like shape. After a short time one ascents to the surface and finds him self in a massive dry cave. Depending on the water level, take off the fins and get to the actual entry. The entry is hard to find as the water is right on top of it and the cave narrows to a restriction. A very appealing cave with rapidly changes depths, it is recommended to dive with a Nitrox blend. After a short while one approaches the main line, further through a narrow tunnel where the cave shows a side tunnel short after which leads to the right in to the deep. Further on the mainline to a opening in the bottom where the line suddenly falls down from 8 meters deep to 23 meters deep. One has to be careful not to disturb the sediment as the walls are covered with the finest cave dust. Without perfect neutral buoyancy there is a risk to the disturb the fine sediment resulting in a complete silt out. This cave system is complex in its shape. Shafts leading from 25 meters deep into sumps make this system very interesting, but only for the experienced cave diver. Equipment configuration: Back mount and Sidemount.

  • latracciaescursioniemontagna.com: https://latracciaescursioniemontagna.com/2022/03/12/676-grotta-dellacqua-nera/ “The origin of the name is unknown, certainly the cave that opens up between the light rocks is black, but the water is completely normal. It is thought to derive from the color of the bottom, covered in dark moss, on which the underground stream flows out before flowing into the Senaiga. Unlike today, it was once always well fed even in periods of drought, raising questions about its origin. In the thirties it was proven, with the introduction of dyes, that the cave is in communication with the Castel Tesino Caves, located at 1000 meters above sea level and a few kilometers away as the crow flies. The fine sand rich in granite crystals sedimented inside the cave indicates a supply of water much further away, coming from the Cima d’Asta Group. This suggests that there is a vast and intricate system of communicating caves inside the mountains.”

“…exploration began only in the 70s by a Speleo diving group from Padua and continued in recent years by a Speleological Group from Valstagna (VI), 1600 meters have been explored overcoming three challenging siphons and many difficult passages.”

item.title: Grotta dell'Orso di Ponte di Nava
item.description:
About

The cave was discovered by chance in October 1886 by the owner of the land while he was excavating for the construction of a wall. The cavity was explored by the owner of the land who found the bone remains of Ursus spelaeus. Hence the name given to the cave. The first systematic exploration was by Capello in 1952, the GSP passed the first siphon upstream in the sixties reaching the next tunnel. In 1991 the CSARI group from Brussels passed a series of siphons reaching a fourth impassable siphon.
